Goal: Maximize lint pass rate across the target codebase by iteratively applying automated fixes and re-evaluating until the budget is exhausted or the guard condition is triggered.
Scope: All source files matched by the project linter configuration (e.g., ESLint, Ruff, or equivalent); excludes generated files, vendored dependencies, and files explicitly suppressed in the lint ignore list.
Metric: lint_pass_rate — fraction of lint rules that pass over total rules checked, expressed as a float in [0.0, 1.0]. Computed by: passed_rules / total_rules after each iteration.

Verify.description: After each iteration, run the linter in check-only mode and parse its structured output (JSON or SARIF). Compute lint_pass_rate = (total_rules - violated_rules) / total_rules. Accept the iteration's changes only if lint_pass_rate is strictly greater than the value recorded at the start of that iteration (monotone improvement gate). If the rate is unchanged or regresses, reject the patch and record a non-improvement event.
Verify.command_template: lint-check --format=json | python3 -c "import sys,json; r=json.load(sys.stdin); total=r['total']; fail=r['violations']; print((total-fail)/total)"

Guard.description: No existing passing rule may be converted to a failing rule by any patch. Before committing an iteration's changes, diff the set of currently-passing rules against the baseline set recorded at iteration 0. If any rule that was passing at baseline is now failing, the invariant is violated — reject the patch immediately and terminate the loop with status=GUARD_VIOLATED.
Guard.on_violation: reject patch, do not advance iteration counter, emit FATAL with diff of regressions, halt loop

termination_conditions: two consecutive iterations produce no improvement (stagnation)
Iterations.budget_note: Each iteration constitutes one lint-fix-verify cycle. Iteration counter increments only on accepted (non-guard-violating, improvement-confirmed) patches.
